q: Dhokla, the spongy steamed gram-flour snack, comes from which state?
note: Often topped with a mustard-seed and curry-leaf tempering and served with green chutney.

q: Litti chokha is a signature dish of which state?
note: Litti are wheat balls stuffed with sattu; chokha is a mash of roasted brinjal, tomato and potato.

q: Vada pav is the iconic street food of which city?
note: Often called the Bombay burger, it was popularised as cheap fast food for mill workers.

q: Wazwan, a lavish multi-course feast, belongs to which region's cuisine?
note: A traditional Wazwan can run to 36 courses, cooked by master chefs called wazas.

q: Which spice gives most Indian curries their yellow colour?
note: Its colour comes from curcumin; India produces most of the world's turmeric.

q: What is the Hindi name for asafoetida?
note: A pinch of hing in hot oil is a classic tempering in dals.

q: Pootharekulu, the paper-thin rolled sweet, comes from which state?
note: Made in Atreyapuram village from rice-starch sheets filled with sugar or jaggery and ghee.

q: Which city is famous for petha, the translucent ash-gourd sweet?
note: Agra's petha shops cluster around the old city, not far from the Taj Mahal.

q: Mysore Pak is made mainly from gram flour, sugar and what?
note: It is said to have been first made in the royal kitchens of Mysore Palace.

q: The Dharwad pedha comes from which state?
note: Its brown colour comes from slow-cooking milk and sugar until it caramelises.

q: Bebinca, a layered coconut-and-egg pudding, is a famous dessert of which state?
note: Often called the queen of Goan desserts, it is a Christmas favourite.

q: In Kolkata, pani puri is usually called what?
note: Gupchup is Odisha's name for it, and pani ke batashe is common in Uttar Pradesh.

q: Sarson da saag is traditionally eaten with which bread?
note: A Punjabi winter classic, often topped with white butter.

q: What is the grand traditional feast served during Onam called?
note: A full sadya can have more than 20 dishes, ending with payasam.

q: Chettinad cuisine, known for its fiery spices, comes from which state?
note: The Chettinad region lies around Karaikudi in Sivaganga district.

q: Which slow-cooked Hyderabadi dish of meat, wheat and lentils is pounded into a thick, porridge-like paste?
note: Hyderabadi haleem was the first meat product in India to get a GI tag, in 2010.

q: Hyderabadi biryani is slow-cooked in a pot sealed with dough. What is this method called?
note: Sealing traps the steam so the rice and meat cook in their own aromas.

q: Pampore in Kashmir is famous for growing which spice?
note: Each saffron thread is a hand-picked stigma of the crocus flower.

q: Ghevar, a disc-shaped honeycomb sweet, is most associated with which state?
note: It is a favourite during Teej and Raksha Bandhan.

q: Tunday Kababi, famous for galouti kebabs, is in which city?
note: Galouti kebabs are minced so finely that they melt in the mouth.

q: Karim's, the famous Mughlai restaurant, is near which Delhi mosque?
note: Karim's opened in 1913 in Old Delhi's Gali Kababian.

q: Bandel cheese, a smoked cheese with Portuguese roots, comes from which state?
note: Named after Bandel in Hooghly district, a former Portuguese settlement.

q: Sandesh, the Bengali sweet, is made primarily from which ingredient?
note: Chhena is fresh cheese made by curdling milk.

q: Which fish, the national fish of Bangladesh, is the pride of Bengali cooking?
note: In Bengal it is famously cooked as shorshe ilish, in a sharp mustard paste.

q: In Kerala's karimeen pollichathu, the fish is cooked wrapped in what?
note: Karimeen is the pearl spot fish, found in Kerala's backwaters.

q: Which Maharashtrian dish is a spicy sprouts curry topped with farsan and eaten with pav?
note: Kolhapur and Pune each have their own famous style of misal.

q: Which Gujarati snack is made of thin gram-flour rolls tempered with mustard seeds?
note: Maharashtra has a very similar snack called suralichi vadi.

q: Undhiyu, a mixed-vegetable winter dish, is a speciality of which state?
note: Its name comes from 'undhu', upside down, as it was cooked in inverted clay pots.

q: Which Madhya Pradesh market sells jewellery by day and turns into a food street at night?
note: Stalls open after the jewellery shops shut, often serving till past midnight.

q: Poha with jalebi is the classic breakfast of which city?
note: Indori poha is often sprinkled with sev and a special spice mix called jeeravan.

q: Which spice is often called the 'king of spices'?
note: Black pepper is native to the Malabar coast; cardamom is called the queen of spices.

q: What is ajwain called in English?
note: Ajwain is often added to parathas and pakoras to aid digestion.

q: What is methi called in English?
note: Both methi leaves and seeds are used; dried leaves are sold as kasuri methi.

q: Saunf, often chewed after meals, is which spice in English?
note: Restaurants often serve it sugar-coated as a mouth freshener.

q: Chhena poda, a baked cheese dessert, comes from which state?
note: Chhena poda literally means 'burnt cheese' in Odia.

q: The bhut jolokia chilli is known in English by what spooky nickname?
note: Guinness World Records named it the world's hottest chilli in 2007.

q: Which Old Delhi lane in Chandni Chowk is famous for fried stuffed parathas?
note: Its shops deep-fry parathas in ghee with fillings from potato to banana.

q: Britannia & Co. in Mumbai is famous for which Parsi rice dish?
note: The dish uses tangy barberries imported from Iran.

q: Which Kolkata neighbourhood is famous as its Chinatown?
note: Tangra's Hakka Chinese community is known for Indian-Chinese dishes like chilli chicken.

q: Which Mumbai dish of mashed spiced vegetables is served with buttered bread rolls?
note: It is said to have started as a quick meal for Mumbai's textile mill workers.

q: Which Kashmiri green tea is brewed with almonds, cardamom and cinnamon?
note: Noon chai, by contrast, is a salty pink tea.

q: Kaju katli is made mainly from which nut?
note: Its diamond shape and silver varq make it a Diwali gift-box staple.

q: Ledikeni, a Bengali sweet, is named after the wife of which Governor-General?
note: It was reportedly created by confectioner Bhim Chandra Nag for Lady Canning.

q: Hapus is the Marathi name for which mango variety?
note: The Alphonso is named after Portuguese general Afonso de Albuquerque.

q: The Banganapalle mango has a GI tag for which state?
note: It is named after the town of Banaganapalle in Nandyal district.

q: Which GI-tagged mango variety is grown around Junagadh and Gir in Gujarat?
note: Its name refers to the saffron colour of its pulp.

q: Modak is said to be the favourite sweet of which deity?
note: Steamed ukadiche modak are made with rice flour, coconut and jaggery.

q: Ven pongal is made mainly from rice and which lentil?
note: It is seasoned with pepper, cumin, ginger and ghee.

q: Which Mughlai dessert of fried bread in thickened milk has a name meaning 'royal piece'?
note: Hyderabad's similar dessert is called double ka meetha.

q: Axone, a fermented soybean ingredient, is a staple of which state's cuisine?
note: Axone is also spelled akhuni and is known for its strong aroma.

q: Pesarattu, a dosa from Andhra Pradesh, is made mainly from which lentil?
note: It is often served with a ginger chutney and upma.

q: Bengal's winter nolen gur is made from the sap of which tree?
note: Nolen gur flavours winter sweets like nolen gurer sandesh.

q: Tandoori chicken gets its name from which kind of clay oven?
note: Tandoors are heated with charcoal or wood and can get extremely hot.

q: Which Delhi restaurant, opened in Daryaganj after Partition, is famous for butter chicken?
note: Moti Mahal's founders first ran an eatery in Peshawar before moving to Delhi.

q: What is the small metal bowl used with a tumbler to serve South Indian filter coffee?
note: Coffee is poured between tumbler and dabarah to cool it and raise a froth.

q: Onam is the harvest festival of which state?
note: Onam celebrates the homecoming of the legendary King Mahabali.

q: The main day of Pongal falls on the first day of which Tamil month?
note: It usually falls on 14 or 15 January, the day after Bhogi.

q: Which festival's name means 'row of lamps'?
note: Homes are lit with diyas, and many regions also draw rangoli at the doorstep.

q: The Hornbill Festival is held every December in which state?
note: It is held at Kisama Heritage Village near Kohima.

q: Which mid-January Punjabi festival is celebrated around a bonfire?
note: People toss rewri, peanuts and popcorn into the fire.

q: Durga Puja is celebrated on the grandest scale in which state?
note: UNESCO added Durga Puja in Kolkata to its Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2021.

q: In Gujarat, Makar Sankranti is famous for kite flying and is called what?
note: Ahmedabad hosts an International Kite Festival around the same time.

q: Which city's Jagannath Temple holds the most famous Rath Yatra?
note: Three huge chariots carry Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra.

q: Which festival celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters with a thread?
note: It falls on the full moon of the month of Shravan.

q: Which Maharashtrian New Year is marked by raising a decorated pole outside homes?
note: The gudi is a pole topped with an upturned pot and bright cloth.

q: Baisakhi is usually celebrated in which month of the Gregorian calendar?
note: It falls on 13 or 14 April and marks the rabi harvest in Punjab.

q: Ugadi marks which occasion in Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh?
note: The name comes from 'yuga' and 'adi', meaning the beginning of a new age.

q: Which Rajasthan town hosts a famous camel fair around Kartik Purnima?
note: Camel races and a moustache contest are among its crowd favourites.

q: Rongali Bihu, which marks the Assamese New Year, is also called what?
note: Assam also celebrates Magh Bihu in January and Kati Bihu in October.

q: Navratri in Gujarat is celebrated with which folk dance performed in circles?
note: Garba is traditionally danced around a lamp or an image of the goddess.

q: What is the bonfire lit on the eve of Holi called?
note: It recalls the story of Prahlad surviving the fire while Holika burned.

q: Lathmar Holi, where women playfully hit men with sticks, is famous in which town?
note: Barsana is traditionally regarded as the village of Radha.

q: Bastar Dussehra in Chhattisgarh is famous for lasting about how many days?
note: It is dedicated to the goddess Danteshwari rather than to Rama.

q: The Kumbh Mela rotates between Prayagraj, Haridwar, Nashik and which city?
note: The Ujjain Kumbh is held on the Shipra river and is called Simhastha.

q: The Mysuru Dasara procession famously features decorated what?
note: The Jamboo Savari elephant carries a golden howdah through the city.

q: The Sangai Festival is held in which state?
note: It is named after the sangai, Manipur's brow-antlered deer.

q: Eid-ul-Fitr marks the end of which month of fasting?
note: The festival begins after the new crescent moon is sighted.

q: Which festival marks Rama's victory over Ravana?
note: Effigies of Ravana are burnt at Ramlila grounds across north India.

q: Tilgul, sesame-jaggery sweets, are exchanged in Maharashtra during which festival?
note: People say 'tilgul ghya, god god bola': take tilgul and speak sweetly.

q: Thekua, a crunchy wheat-and-jaggery cookie, is a key offering during which festival?
note: During Chhath, devotees offer arghya to the setting and rising sun.

q: Kathakali is the classical dance-drama of which state?
note: Performers train for years to control even their eye movements.

q: Kuchipudi takes its name from a village in which state?
note: Kuchipudi village is in Krishna district.

q: Which classical dance of Tamil Nadu was earlier known as Sadir?
note: It was renamed and revived on the concert stage in the 1930s.

q: The Sattriya classical dance originated in which state?
note: It was introduced by the Vaishnava saint Srimanta Sankardev (1449-1568).

q: Ghoomar is a folk dance most associated with which state?
note: Dancers spin so their long ghagras flare out in circles.

q: Lavani, performed to the beat of the dholki, is a folk form of which state?
note: Lavani dancers usually wear a nine-yard saree.

q: Yakshagana, a colourful dance-drama with elaborate headgear, is from which state?
note: It is most popular in the coastal districts of Karnataka.

q: Madhubani painting comes from which state?
note: It is also called Mithila painting, after the region where it developed.

q: Warli painting is the art of a tribe from which state?
note: Warli art uses simple circles, triangles and lines, traditionally in white on mud walls.

q: Raghurajpur, a heritage village famous for Pattachitra painting, is in which state?
note: Almost every household in Raghurajpur practises a craft, from pattachitra to palm-leaf engraving.

q: In Kalamkari textile art, what does the word 'kalam' mean?
note: Artisans draw with a bamboo pen dipped in natural dyes.

q: Tanjore paintings are famous for their use of what?
note: The style flourished under Maratha rulers of Thanjavur.

q: Kanjeevaram silk sarees are woven in which state?
note: They come from Kanchipuram, known for heavy silk and zari borders.

q: Pochampally ikat weaving comes from which present-day state?
note: Pochampally ikat was among the first Indian products to receive a GI tag.

q: Pashmina wool comes from Changthangi goats of which region?
note: The goats grow the fine undercoat to survive winters on the Changthang plateau.

q: What is the double-ikat silk saree woven in Patan, Gujarat called?
note: In double ikat, both warp and weft threads are tie-dyed before weaving.

q: Chikankari embroidery is most associated with which city?
note: Traditionally it is white thread embroidery on fine muslin.

q: Phulkari embroidery comes from which state?
note: Phulkari means 'flower work', stitched in bright silk floss.

q: Channapatna in Karnataka is famous for what kind of toys?
note: Channapatna is nicknamed 'Gombegala Ooru', the town of toys.

q: Moradabad is known as the 'City of' which metal?
note: Its brass handicrafts are exported worldwide, earning it the name Peetal Nagri.

q: Dhokra metal craft is made using which technique?
note: Mohenjo-daro's Dancing Girl bronze was made with the same lost-wax method.

q: Blue pottery is a famous craft of which city?
note: It is made from quartz-based paste rather than clay.

q: In Kathakali, a green face (pacha) usually represents which kind of character?
note: Characters like Krishna and Arjuna are shown in pacha make-up.

q: Odissi is the classical dance of which state?
note: Temple sculptures at Konark show poses similar to Odissi.

q: Chhau, a masked martial dance, is performed in West Bengal, Jharkhand and which other state?
note: Chhau was added to UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010.

q: Which script is used to write Punjabi in India?
note: Gurmukhi was standardised by the second Sikh Guru, Guru Angad.

q: Which script is used to write Hindi?
note: Marathi, Nepali and Sanskrit are also commonly written in Devanagari.

q: Which language was the first to be declared a classical language of India, in 2004?
note: Sanskrit followed in 2005.

q: In which year were Marathi, Bengali, Assamese, Pali and Prakrit declared classical languages?
note: This took India's list of classical languages to eleven.

q: Konkani is the official language of which state?
note: Konkani is also spoken along the coasts of Karnataka and Maharashtra.

q: The Meitei (Manipuri) language has its own script. What is it called?
note: The script has been revived and taught in Manipur's schools in recent decades.

q: According to the 2011 Census, which language has India's second-most native speakers?
note: Hindi was first; Marathi and Telugu came third and fourth.

q: The Trinity of Carnatic music is Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and who?
note: All three were born in Tiruvarur, Tamil Nadu, in the 18th century.

q: Ustad Bismillah Khan was a master of which instrument?
note: He received the Bharat Ratna in 2001.

q: Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is famous for playing which instrument?
note: The bansuri is a side-blown bamboo flute.

q: What is Kerala's traditional cream saree with a gold zari border called?
note: 'Kasavu' is the name for the gold zari border itself.

q: The mekhela chador is traditional attire from which state?
note: The finest ones are woven in golden muga silk.

q: What is the traditional string-puppet theatre of Rajasthan called?
note: 'Kath' means wood and 'putli' means doll.

q: Gond painting is a tribal art form from which state?
note: Patangarh village in Dindori district is its best-known centre.

q: In Tamil Nadu, the rice-flour floor designs similar to rangoli are called what?
note: Alpana is Bengal's version, and muggu is the Telugu one.

q: Who is traditionally credited as the author of the Ramayana?
note: Valmiki is honoured as the 'adi kavi', the first poet.

q: Who is traditionally credited with composing the Mahabharata?
note: His full name is Krishna Dvaipayana Vyasa.

q: According to legend, who acted as the scribe and wrote down the Mahabharata as it was dictated?
note: The scribe's condition was that the dictation must never pause.

q: What is the name of Arjuna's bow?
note: Arjuna received the Gandiva from Agni before the burning of the Khandava forest.

q: Who was the eldest of the five Pandava brothers?
note: Yudhishthira was known as Dharmaraja for his commitment to truth.

q: Who was Karna's birth mother?
note: She set the infant Karna afloat on a river in a basket.

q: In the Ramayana, Ravana was the king of which kingdom?
note: Lanka was said to be a city of gold.

q: What was the name of Ravana's flying chariot?
note: Ravana had seized the Pushpaka from his half-brother Kubera.

q: Which brother of Rama accompanied him into exile?
note: Lakshmana's wife Urmila stayed back in Ayodhya.

q: For how many years was Rama exiled to the forest?
note: The Pandavas' exile was 12 years plus one year in hiding.

q: Which sister of Ravana, humiliated in the Panchavati forest, urged him to abduct Sita?
note: Her name is usually explained as 'one with nails like winnowing baskets'.

q: Which vulture king tried to stop Ravana from carrying Sita away?
note: Sampati was Jatayu's elder brother.

q: Which brother of Ravana left him to join Rama's side?
note: Vibhishana is counted among the Chiranjivis, the legendary immortals.

q: Which monkey king, brother of Vali, became Rama's ally?
note: Sugriva ruled the monkey kingdom of Kishkindha.

q: Which guru of the Pandavas and Kauravas was the father of Ashwatthama?
note: Arjuna was his favourite pupil.

q: Who was the eldest of the Kaurava brothers?
note: The Kauravas are traditionally counted as a hundred brothers.

q: Who narrated the Kurukshetra war to the blind king Dhritarashtra?
note: He was granted divine sight so he could see the battlefield from afar.

q: How many days did the Kurukshetra war last?
note: The Bhagavad Gita also has 18 chapters.

q: Which Kuru elder had the boon of choosing the time of his own death?
note: Bhishma lay on a bed of arrows until the sun began its northward journey.

q: Which Pandava was famous for his great strength and huge appetite?
note: Bhima's favourite weapon was the gada, or mace.

q: Abhimanyu was killed after entering which battle formation?
note: He knew how to break into it but not how to get out.

q: Karna's father was which god?
note: Indra was Arjuna's divine father, Vayu was Bhima's and Yama was Yudhishthira's.

q: What is the name of Shiva's trident?
note: Shiva also carries the damaru, a small hourglass-shaped drum.

q: What is the name of Vishnu's spinning discus?
note: Pinaka is Shiva's bow, Vajra is Indra's weapon and Kaumodaki is Vishnu's mace.

q: Lord Ganesha's vahana, or mount, is which animal?
note: The mount's name is usually given as Mushika or Mooshak.

q: Which bird is the vahana of Lord Vishnu?
note: The peacock carries Kartikeya, the swan carries Saraswati and the owl carries Lakshmi.

q: The Panchatantra is traditionally attributed to which scholar?
note: Panchatantra means 'five treatises', and it has five books.

q: According to its frame story, the Panchatantra was composed to teach whom?
note: The king in the frame story is Amarashakti, and the teacher promised to educate his sons within six months.

q: The Jataka tales are stories about the previous lives of whom?
note: There are around 550 Jataka tales in the Pali tradition.

q: Which demon king was killed by Vishnu's Narasimha avatar?
note: Hiranyakashipu's son Prahlad was a devotee of Vishnu.

q: Which avatar of Vishnu took the form of a boar?
note: Matsya was a fish, Kurma a tortoise and Vamana a dwarf.

q: During their year in hiding, what name did Arjuna use as a dance teacher?
note: Kanka was Yudhishthira's disguise, Ballava was Bhima's and Sairandhri was Draupadi's.

q: The Pandavas spent their year incognito at the court of which king?
note: Virata ruled the Matsya kingdom; his daughter Uttara later married Abhimanyu.

q: Indra's weapon, the Vajra, was made from the bones of which sage?
note: Indra needed the Vajra to defeat the demon Vritra.

q: Which king did penance to bring the river Ganga down to earth?
note: Shiva caught Ganga in his hair to soften her fall.

q: In the Ramayana, who was Sita's father?
note: Janaka was king of Mithila, which is why Sita is also called Maithili.

q: Which brother of Rama ruled Ayodhya with Rama's sandals placed on the throne?
note: Bharata ruled from Nandigram as Rama's representative.

q: Which demon disguised himself as a golden deer to lure Rama away?
note: Ravana abducted Sita while Rama chased the deer.

q: Ravana's son Meghnad is better known by which name earned by defeating Indra?
note: He was feared for fighting invisibly from behind the clouds using magic.

q: Which brother of Ravana famously slept for six months at a time?
note: Legend says he asked for 'nidrasana', a bed, instead of 'indrasana', Indra's throne.

q: In which year did Rabindranath Tagore win the Nobel Prize in Literature?
note: He was the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.

q: What is the name of the fictional town in R.K. Narayan's stories?
note: Malgudi Days became a much-loved Doordarshan series in 1986.

q: Which was R.K. Narayan's first novel, published in 1935?
note: Graham Greene helped get it published in England.

q: Which R.K. Narayan novel follows Raju, a tour guide mistaken for a holy man?
note: It won the Sahitya Akademi Award and inspired the 1965 film Guide.

q: Which Premchand novel follows the poor farmer Hori and his wife Dhania?
note: Published in 1936, it was Premchand's last completed novel.

q: What was Munshi Premchand's real name?
note: He first wrote in Urdu under the pen name Nawab Rai.

q: Which novel about Rusty, a teenage orphan in Dehradun, won the John Llewellyn Rhys Prize?
note: It was Ruskin Bond's first novel, begun when he was 17.

q: Which Chetan Bhagat novel was the basis for the film '3 Idiots'?
note: Five Point Someone, published in 2004, is set at IIT Delhi.

q: The film 'Kai Po Che!' was adapted from which Chetan Bhagat novel?
note: The novel follows three friends in Ahmedabad who start a cricket shop.

q: Which Chetan Bhagat novel is about a Punjabi boy marrying a Tamil girl?
alt: 2 States: The Story of My Marriage
note: The couple, Krish and Ananya, meet while studying at IIM Ahmedabad.

q: Who won the 1997 Booker Prize for 'The God of Small Things'?
note: It was her debut novel, set in Aymanam, Kerala.

q: Which novel won Salman Rushdie the 1981 Booker Prize?
note: It was later named the 'Booker of Bookers' in 1993.

q: Kiran Desai won the 2006 Booker Prize for which novel?
note: Her mother, Anita Desai, was shortlisted for the Booker three times.

q: Aravind Adiga won the 2008 Booker Prize for which novel?
note: It was Adiga's debut novel, narrated by Balram Halwai.

q: In which year did Geetanjali Shree's 'Tomb of Sand' win the International Booker Prize?
note: It was the first book translated from Hindi to win; Daisy Rockwell translated it.

q: Who wrote the novel 'Train to Pakistan'?
note: It is set in the fictional border village of Mano Majra.

q: In which Vikram Seth novel does Mrs Rupa Mehra look for a husband for her daughter Lata?
note: Published in 1993, it is one of the longest novels in English.

q: Amitav Ghosh's 'Sea of Poppies' begins which trilogy?
note: The trilogy is named after the ship Ibis; it continues with River of Smoke and Flood of Fire.

q: Who wrote the Hindi poetry collection 'Madhushala'?
note: Harivansh Rai Bachchan was the father of actor Amitabh Bachchan.

q: Who wrote 'Rashmirathi', the Hindi epic poem about Karna?
note: Dinkar won the Jnanpith Award in 1972 for 'Urvashi'.

q: Which Sanskrit poet wrote 'Meghaduta', in which a cloud carries a message?
note: In the poem, an exiled yaksha sends the cloud to his wife.

q: Which Sanskrit play tells the love story of King Dushyanta and Shakuntala?
note: A ring given by Dushyanta is key to the plot.

q: Who wrote the novel 'Devdas'?
note: Devdas was published in 1917 and has been filmed many times.

q: Who wrote the Bengali novel 'Pather Panchali'?
note: Satyajit Ray's Apu Trilogy was based on this novel and its sequel.

q: Which fictional detective did Satyajit Ray create?
note: Feluda's real name is Prodosh Chandra Mitter, and his cousin Topshe narrates.

q: Who wrote 'The Palace of Illusions', the Mahabharata told by Draupadi?
note: It was published in 2008.

q: 'The Immortals of Meluha' is the first book in whose Shiva Trilogy?
note: The trilogy continues with The Secret of the Nagas and The Oath of the Vayuputras.

q: Which Jhumpa Lahiri book won the 2000 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction?
note: It was her debut short-story collection.

q: Who wrote 'The Great Indian Novel', a satire retelling the Mahabharata?
note: Published in 1989, it recasts Indian political history through the epic.

q: Which Tamil epic tells the story of Kannagi and her anklet?
note: It is attributed to the prince-poet Ilango Adigal.

q: Which classic Tamil text of 1,330 couplets did Thiruvalluvar write?
note: It is divided into three parts: virtue, wealth and love.

q: Which poet wrote the 'Ramcharitmanas'?
note: He wrote it in the 16th century in Awadhi, a dialect of Hindi.

q: Who wrote 'Sultana's Dream' (1905), an early feminist science-fiction story?
note: It imagines Ladyland, a country where women run everything.

q: Which poet was known as the 'Nightingale of India'?
note: Her poetry collections include 'The Golden Threshold' and 'The Bird of Time'.

q: Which Malayalam writer wrote 'Randamoozham', the Mahabharata retold through Bhima?
note: The title means 'the second turn', as Bhima was always second in line.

q: Who wrote the Malayalam novel 'Chemmeen'?
note: Chemmeen, about a fishing community, was published in 1956.

q: The first Jnanpith Award, in 1965, went to a writer in which language?
note: It went to G. Sankara Kurup for his poetry collection 'Odakkuzhal'.

q: Who wrote 'The Blue Umbrella'?
note: The story's heroine is Binya, a girl from a Garhwal village.

q: In Premchand's story 'Idgah', what does young Hamid buy for his grandmother?
note: He buys a chimta so she won't burn her fingers making rotis.
